tip: на (na = on) takes the prepositional case for location: на столе (na stole = on the table). The base form стол (stol) shifts to столе.
Нет (net = there isn't) forces genitive: ничего невозможного (nichego nevozmozhnogo = nothing impossible), not a nominative form.
Откуда (otkuda = from where) asks where motion starts, куда (kuda = where to) asks the destination. Both go with motion verbs.
картой (kartoy = by card) is instrumental: paying by means of something uses the instrumental form with no preposition. Base карта (karta) becomes картой.
Что это за (chto eto za = what kind of) keeps the noun nominative: что это за здание (zdanie = building), not a genitive form.
по-русски (po-russki = in Russian) is an adverb, not a noun. Use it with говорю (govoryu = speak); there is no separate word for the language itself.
ничего (nichego = nothing) still needs не (ne = not) on the verb: ничего не понимаю (ne ponimayu = don't understand). Russian keeps both negatives.
домой (domoy = homeward) marks motion toward home. Being at home would be дома (doma = at home). Different words for going versus being.
Куда (kuda = where to) asks about direction and pairs with motion verbs like ведёт (vedyot = leads).
Какое (kakoe = what a) is neuter, matching здание (zdanie = building). красивое (krasivoe) agrees in neuter too; a masculine noun would take какой (kakoy).
бегает (begaet = runs) is the habitual form for repeated action, fitting каждое утро (kazhdoe utro = every morning). One run in progress would be бежит (bezhit).
два (dva = two) takes genitive singular: два года (dva goda = two years), not the plural годы (gody). Numbers 2, 3, 4 all do this.
один (odin = one) keeps the noun nominative singular: двадцать один год (dvadtsat odin god = twenty-one years), not года (goda). Any number ending in 1 does this.
Сколько (skolko = how much) takes genitive: сколько времени (skolko vremeni = how much time). The base время (vremya) shifts to времени.
музыку (muzyku = music) is the object form of музыка (muzyka). Feminine nouns change their ending when they are the direct object.
хорошего вечера (khoroshego vechera = good evening) uses genitive: good wishes are stated in the genitive, literally 'of a good evening', not nominative.
размер обуви (razmer obuvi = shoe size): the second noun goes genitive to mean 'size of footwear'. Base обувь (obuv) becomes обуви.
с (s = with) takes instrumental: с твоей машиной (s tvoey mashinoy = with your car). Base машина (mashina) becomes машиной.
Чей (chey = whose) is masculine to match зонтик (zontik = umbrella). A feminine noun would take чья (chya) instead.
даже если (dazhe esli = even if) introduces a concession: даже если болеет (bolejet = is sick), he still works.
свои (svoi = one's own) points back to the subject and matches the thing owned: свои мечты (svoi mechty = one's own dreams).
Мне (mne = to me) is dative: age is stated with dative, literally 'to me thirty-two years', not with я (ya = I).
помочь (pomoch = to help) takes dative with no word for 'to': помочь вам (pomoch vam = help you). вам is the dative of вы (vy = you).
